verdict.rationale: Auth0's 'Auth0 for AI' line explicitly positions the product to let agents 'connect to MCP servers more securely' and to secure agent-to-API calls with OAuth 2.0, delegated authorization, and CIBA (auth0-docs-20, auth0-docs-68, auth0-docs-16, auth0-docs-78), showing the vendor markets exactly this use case. However, the evidence is largely repeated marketing taglines rather than a concrete technical walkthrough of standing up a spec-compliant OAuth authorization server in front of a self-built MCP resource server (e.g., dynamic client registration, resource-indicator/audience-scoped tokens per the MCP auth spec), and there is no independent/hands-on corroboration that this flow works end-to-end for remote agent connections. Missing for 10: a concrete implementation guide showing MCP-spec-compliant OAuth (PKCE, dynamic client registration, resource indicators) protecting a third-party MCP server, and independent verification of scoped/verifiable token issuance in practice.
